issue_context.title: rhsm_subscription doesn't clear cache leading to yum_package failures
issue_context.body:
## Description

When you attach to a new subscription using the `rhsm_subscription` resource and then the `package` resource to install something sourced from that subscription it fails.

## Chef Version

v15.3.8

## Platform Version

Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.8

## Replication Case


```ruby
rhsm_subscription 'pool_id_goes_here'

package 'package_from_subscription'
```

I wish I could give a publicly available example but my use case is a private RPM in our internal Red Hat Satellite server.

## Client Output
<!--- The relevant output of the chef-client run or a link to a gist of the entire run, if there is one.

The debug output (chef-client -l debug) may be useful, but please link to a gist, or truncate it. -->

```text
           * No candidate version available for package_from_subscription
           ================================================================================
           Error executing action `install` on resource 'yum_package[package_from_subscription]'
           ================================================================================

           Chef::Exceptions::Package
           -------------------------
           No candidate version available for package_from_subscription

           Resource Declaration:
           ---------------------
           # In /tmp/kitchen/cache/cookbooks/test-cookbook/recipes/default.rb
            33: package 'package_from_subscription'
            34: 

           Compiled Resource:
           ------------------
           # Declared in /tmp/kitchen/cache/cookbooks/test-cookbook/recipes/default.rb:33:in `from_file'
           yum_package("package_from_subscription") do
             package_name "package_from_subscription"
             action [:install]
             default_guard_interpreter :default
             declared_type :package
             cookbook_name "test-cookbook"
             recipe_name "default"

```

@lamont-granquist should probably chime in on how to reload the cache there.

`instance.restart` is what you'd need, which is what `flush_cache` calls (which is the workaround which is to send a `:flush_cache` event to any package provider as a notify from the rhsm_subscription resource)

review_comments: @lamont-granquist I am unable to figure out why this isn't working properly. When I run the unit tests it's still trying to run `#shell_out!` on the actual host instead of rspec catching it and responding with the mock.
@lamont-granquist  Will this also run the default action (i.e. `:install`)? Or is this all good?

In other words, do I need to do this?

```ruby
build_resource(:package, "rhsm_subscription-#{new_resource.pool_id}-flush_cache") do
  action :nothing
end.run_action(:flush_cache)
```

no you're not using `declare_resource` so its not being put on the resource_collection and won't be converged by the normal process.  only the actions you run get run.

`build_resource` is just some magic around getting a `new` instance of the right package resource.

This also means that it won't cause the resource you are running to be updated when it updates -- which is why you shouldn't generally ever use build_resource and should at least use declare_resource -- but here we're doing it deliberately because we're flushing the cache and that has nothing to do with the underlying state of the machine changing.  Arguably using a resource for this is philosophically wrong, but its the public API that we have.
